clue.text: More than sufficient drink to drown one at a sitting?

indicators.note: the drink swamps and surrounds the other piece, so one sits within it

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
an MP, Member of Parliament, attends sittings of the House

explanation.surface: Someone downs a generous drink in one go at a single session.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' flags that 'one at a sitting' is not a single gulp but a parliamentarian, who attends sittings of the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful, more than enough, is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Worker on leading edge in rock formation

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
IC, in charge, means leading
a line can mark an edge or boundary

explanation.surface: A labourer at the front edge of a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists use the term for an arch-shaped fold of rock strata.

clue.text: Question one who faces the camera?

explanation.surface: Ask about the model.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling question is a poser; someone who strikes poses for a photographer is one too.

clue.text: Record one priest as a person by no means ascetic

definitions.text: a person by no means ascetic

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one
a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A recording of a priest is cited as proof he is no hermit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet devoted to fine eating is the opposite of a self-denying ascetic.

clue.text: State call to imprison journalist has faded

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for Washington State (or Western Australia)

indicators.note: the call locks up the journalist, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to shout is to call out
ED, editor, a standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An official declaration jailing a reporter has lost its force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning declare, but it is a US or Australian state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours that are washed out have lost intensity, i.e. faded.

clue.text: The sound of a horse or a bear heard by some?

indicators.note: spoken by those who drop the H, the two words sound the same

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is a famous bear

explanation.surface: A neigh, or perhaps a growl, depending on the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard by some' signals a sound-alike that works only for speakers who don't aspirate WH.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's gentle neigh is its characteristic noise.

clue.text: Four bound by cord putting up a fight

indicators.note: tied up inside, so the number sits within the cord

parts.note: string is cord
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people tied up with rope resist.
explanation.definitionFit: Struggling hard against opposition is putting up a fight.

clue.text: Flower-holder Green Peace ordered, having lost the last one

indicators.note: put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
the word drops its closing letters

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners ordered a vase, then lost the final one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost the last one' cuts ACE from PEACE, leaving PE; 'ordered' rearranges GREEN + PE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental table centrepiece with dishes or vases for fruit and flowers.

clue.text: Capsizes open vessels

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
urns are vessels

explanation.surface: Open boats keel over.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn upside down, as a boat capsizes.

clue.text: Like certain architecture for a royal house

explanation.surface: Describing a palace's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Tudor names a style of English building with half-timbering, and the dynasty of Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Exam condition that is right one declares

parts.note: a test is an exam
if introduces a condition
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A test with a proviso, which is right, makes someone a witness.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who testifies makes a solemn statement, as a witness does in court.

clue.text: In retrospect, the word Nemesis is not wholly correct

indicators.note: In retrospect says the hidden letters are read backwards, looking back
only part of the words is taken, so a run sits inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looking back, a remark about Nemesis turns out to be partly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'is not wholly correct' as the definition, but that phrase cannot replace a verb meaning put right; 'is not wholly' signals the hidden run DNEME, which 'In retrospect' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to put its errors right.

clue.text: Naughty vicar a-courting embraces maiden — Rose, perhaps

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hug the extra piece, which sits inside
naughty behaviour is disorderly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A mischievous clergyman goes wooing and hugs a young woman named Rose.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Alec Rose sailed single-handed round the world in 1967-68; Rose looks like a girl's name being courted.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec Rose is an example of a round-the-world sailor.

clue.text: One gets cross with insects around, the giddy creatures!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the insects surround the cross

parts.note: bees are insects
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry with bees buzzing round, the silly things!
explanation.walkthrough: Ibexes are mountain goats living at dizzy heights, hence 'giddy'. 'around' puts X inside BEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild mountain goats that live on sheer crags would be giddy if heights affected them.

clue.text: Offhand old secretary, a lump not completely worthless?

parts.note: ex means former, old
a temp is a temporary secretary
a lump of rock containing some valuable metal

explanation.surface: A careless remark about a former secretary as a bit of a waste.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' marks a cryptic hint: a lump of rock that has some metal in it is not entirely worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without preparation, spontaneously, as an impromptu speech.

clue.text: Altering dubiously a mathematical quantity

indicators.note: done in a questionable way, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Changing a calculation in a shady way.
explanation.definitionFit: In calculus an integral is a quantity found by integration.

clue.text: Being in trouble, Adam helps make a sort of cover

indicators.note: letters in a mess are rearranged

explanation.surface: Adam, in difficulty, gets help making something to cover up.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade over a light bulb is a kind of cover.

clue.text: National Conservative includes a word for the floaters

indicators.note: the two words hold the next letter between them

parts.note: Nat is short for National
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative nationalist adopts a term for drifting voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floaters' suggests undecided voters; here it means swimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Natatory means relating to or adapted for swimming.

clue.text: Public school type espousing Socialism initially — a Republican?

indicators.note: taking as a spouse, so the school type holds the letter within

parts.note: an Etonian went to Eton, a famous English public (private fee-paying) school

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An Old Etonian embracing socialism: surely not a Republican?
explanation.walkthrough: 'espousing' puts S inside ETONIAN. Republican means a citizen of a republic, here Estonia, not a US party member.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Estonia belongs to a Baltic republic, so is an example of a republican.

clue.text: Bits of food eaten finally, lots

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: oodles means lots

explanation.surface: Morsels of food were eaten at last, in great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Strips of pasta are pieces of food.

clue.text: Light wood beginning to mellow is fragrant

parts.note: balsa is a very light wood

indicators.note: only the start of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A light timber that starts to mature smells sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: balsam is a fragrant resin, a noun, so 'fragrant' stands for the sweet-smelling substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is an aromatic resinous substance, prized for its sweet scent.

clue.text: A tree conservationists used to provide food

parts.note: lime is a tree
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Environmentalists used a tree to provide nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment or sustenance is aliment.

clue.text: I've got the point!

parts.note: a fencer's cry acknowledging a hit, and a concession in argument

explanation.definitionFit: Fencers call this French exclamation when hit; in debate it concedes a clever riposte.

clue.text: A seventeenth-century drama to bring the house down?

definitions.text: A seventeenth-century drama to bring the house down?

parts.words: A seventeenth-century drama to bring the house down?
parts.note: a play from the 1600s whose hero literally brings a building crashing down, rather than winning applause

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's 1671 verse drama tells how the blinded Israelite strongman pulled down the Philistine temple; 'bring the house down' usually means getting huge applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's tragedy is a seventeenth-century drama about the strongman who toppled the Philistines' temple.

clue.text: Cloth required when there's sign of injury on female

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on the second

parts.note: a scar marks an old injury

explanation.surface: Bandage needed when a woman is wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarf is a length of cloth worn around the neck.

clue.text: Sort of appeal going up to bear Goliath?

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: IT is sex appeal
tan means beat, as in tan someone's hide

explanation.surface: An appeal mounted to defend the giant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns IT into TI. Goliath is the giant of the Bible, so a type of giant.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was a giant, and a titan is a giant of great size or power.

clue.text: Sea rocks getting a number killed

parts.note: the death toll is the number killed

explanation.surface: Rocks at sea claim a toll of lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A coral reef ring enclosing a lagoon is a formation of rocks at sea.

clue.text: Yellow box used by artist, part of it brass

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
a chest is a box
RA, Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter keeps a yellow box, partly made of brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of it brass' looks like a description of the box; it defines a body of musicians with a brass section.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony ensemble includes a section of brass instruments.

clue.text: Public wants elegance in swimming event

parts.note: free, as in a free library, open to the public without charge
style is elegance

explanation.surface: Ordinary people want some grace in a race at the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Front-crawl races where any stroke is allowed are a standard swimming race.

clue.text: Maybe past being anxious

explanation.surface: Possibly beyond worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the past is one verb form of time; anxious also means strained, on edge.
